newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: Bolivia threatens Spanish-run pension funds.
newsitem.headline: Bolivia threatens Spanish-run pension funds.

text.p: Bolivia threatened the country's only two private pension funds, both owned by Spanish banks, with government intervention Thursday if they refuse to sign up millions of dollars of shares to a social trust fund.

The pension firms, Argentaria's AFP Futuro and Banco Bilbao Vizcaya's Prevision, have only been in operation since May but are already in a fierce dispute with the government over a decree last month ordering them to set up a five-year trust to guarantee funds for social programs.

"If the pension funds don't obey government orders, the only thing the Pension Regulator's Office can do is, as the law says, to intervene them," said regulator Guillero Aponte after talks with President Gonzalo Sanchez de Lozada.

The government had set a Wednesday night deadline for the funds to set up a trust with Citibank's Cititrust in the Bahamas with about $1.6 billion of privately-held shares in former state companies sold off in the past three years.

But the pension funds argue that these funds are the mainstay of their operations and they wrote to Bolivia's Capitalization Minister Alfonso Revollo Thursday saying they would not sign anything until the Supreme Court decides on an appeal against the trust decree -- an appeal lodged by the political opposition which takes power on August 6.
